sources.title: Party walls and building work: Overview
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: Party wall duties apply to specified shared-boundary work and are distinct from planning permission or building regulations approval.

sources.title: Party walls and building work: Work you must tell your neighbour about
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: Notice duties depend on the actual boundary, party structure and excavation relationship; no sample parcel is assumed to trigger them.

sources.title: Party walls and building work: When and how to tell them
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: Notice timing and written content are project-specific and cannot be inferred from borough or parcel context alone.

sources.title: Party walls and building work: Reaching an agreement with your neighbours
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: Consent, counter-notice and dispute routes depend on actual notices and neighbour responses; silence is not treated as consent.

sources.title: Party walls and building work: If you cannot agree
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: A surveyor and party wall award may be required after a dispute; this does not establish that a sample parcel has a dispute or award.

sources.title: Party walls and building work: When works begin
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: Duties during works include avoiding unnecessary inconvenience and dealing with damage; access provisions arise only within the statutory process.

sources.title: Preventing and resolving disputes in relation to party walls
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: The official publication gathers Party Wall Act guidance and example notices; generic templates do not prove a candidate-specific legal relationship.

sources.title: The Party Wall etc Act 1996: explanatory booklet
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: The booklet is general guidance rather than an authoritative court interpretation and requires project-specific facts for application.
